# Changing the board

If `board` answers that it finds no configuration, this repository has no
board yet: `board init` makes one, and that is the only step to offer.

Work items are moved with `board set`; this is for when the value you need
does not exist.

The board owns what it is now: every read uses the shape the last sync found,
including whatever was added in the browser. Config owns the minimum a board
must have — the columns, fields and views the skills rely on — and is what
`board admin apply` builds, not an inventory. So an option, a label or a view
someone adds as the work needs it is not missing from config, and is not
yours to declare there unless asked. Both go through config: the board's shape is declared in
the repo's boardkit config and applied, never clicked together in the browser, so the next
repo that runs `board admin apply` gets the same board.

## What this board has now

`board` prints the items and the columns they sit in; `board json` carries
every field value. Read that before adding anything, so a field that exists
under another name is not added twice.

## Adding something

Edit the `[board]` section of the repo's boardkit config, then apply:

```toml
[board]
status_order = ["Inbox", "Todo", "In Progress", "Done"]   # the columns, in order

[board.fields.area]
data_type = "SINGLE_SELECT"   # or TEXT, NUMBER, DATE, MULTI_SELECT, ITERATION
options = ["Core", "API", "UI", "Infra", "Docs", "Tests"]

[[board.views]]
name = "Current"
layout = "BOARD"
fields = ["status", "area"]

[[board.views]]
name = "All"
layout = "TABLE"
fields = ["status", "area"]
```

```bash
board admin apply -n                  # preview missing shape
board admin apply                     # add it; preserve existing views
board admin apply --reconcile -n      # preview declared view updates
board admin apply --reconcile         # make declared layouts and filters win
board admin apply --prune-views -n    # preview which stray tabs would go
board admin apply --prune-views       # delete tabs config does not name
board sync                            # pull the new shape into the snapshot
```

## Starting from a preset

A preset is a board shape boardkit ships, and presets stack:

- `work` is doing the work in the repository: the columns above, `blocked`,
  Current (the work, as a board) and All. `board init` writes it.
- `pm` builds on `work` with planning and reporting: `start` and `target`
  dates, Roadmap (the Initiatives, with progress and milestone), Timeline (the
  work along time, by parent) and Initiatives (the roadmap along time).

- `portfolio` is a board of other boards: the Initiatives of the
  repositories listed under `[portfolio] repos`, with their dates, in one
  organisation's view. It builds on nothing. See "A portfolio" below.

Name one under `[board]`:

```toml
[board]
preset = "pm"
```

Anything the repo declares beside it wins by name — a view called `Current`
replaces the preset's — and anything else it declares is added. `board admin
apply --preset pm` applies a preset to an existing board for one run,
adding only what is missing; add the line to keep it.

A preset needs a few settings the API cannot make: a view's grouping, sort and
date fields, and the Project workflows. `board init` and `board admin apply`
end by printing them as numbered steps, each with a link. You cannot click
them, and nothing tells boardkit whether they were done, so give that list to
the person word for word, links included, as the last thing in your reply. Do
not summarise it or say the board is ready without it. `board admin checklist`
prints it again, whenever someone asks how to finish the board.

These run under the repository's own credential. Creating a project reaches
beyond it, so `board admin apply` refuses and asks for `--as-me`, which uses
the person's own gh login. Ask the person before adding `--as-me`; never add it
to get past a refusal on your own.

## A portfolio

A portfolio lives in a repository of its own. `board init --preset portfolio`
writes its config and the daily Action that runs `board portfolio sync`.
Which repositories it covers is the one thing to edit:

```toml
[portfolio]
repos = ["web-app", "data-pipeline"]
```

```bash
board portfolio sync -n     # what it would add, copy or remove
board portfolio sync        # do it; the Action does this every morning
```

The sync is the only thing that writes to a portfolio. Its items are copies,
so a date or a status is changed on the Initiative's own board, never on the
portfolio. A portfolio covers one organisation: its Project can hold no
other's issues.

## What apply will and will not do

It adds: a missing field, a missing option, a missing view. It renames an
option that differs from config only in case, keeping the items in it.

By default, an existing view stays as GitHub holds it. `--reconcile` also
updates layouts and filters on declared views. Use it only when the board's
shape is deliberately managed from config; preview it with `-n` first.

`--prune-views` deletes the saved tabs config does not name, and is the only
deletion boardkit performs — a view holds no items and no field values, so
what is lost is the grouping and sorting config cannot express. It is a
separate flag from `--reconcile` and is never implied by it. A field, an
option and a column are never deleted. Ask before pruning a board you do not
own: a tab you did not declare may be someone's working filter, and GitHub has
no undo. Preview with `-n` and say which tabs would go.

## Native GitHub workflows

GitHub does not expose supported create or update operations for Project
workflows. Configure these once in the Project's **Workflows** settings:

- When Status becomes `Done`, close the issue.
- Auto-archive items matching `is:closed reason:"not planned"`.

These are mechanical consequences of the board shape. Work-item acceptance
still belongs to the `board` skill.

Apply alone never deletes. A field, option or view the board has and config
does not is left alone, because deleting an option discards the value every item holds in
it. So removing something is a decision taken in the browser, by someone who
can see what is in it.

Two options differing only in case are reported rather than merged: moving
items between columns is a change to contents, not shape.

## When a sync reports drift

`board sync` says when config declares a field or an option the board does
not have. Boards are edited in the browser, so this is ordinary, not an error.

It is a person's call which side is right, so report it and ask; do not
settle it to make the warning go away. When you recommend, default to fixing
the config — delete the line from `[board]` — because someone changed the
board deliberately, and recreating what they removed puts back a column they
wanted gone.

Run `board admin apply` instead only when the config line is new — written to
create something and not yet applied.

## After changing the shape

```bash
board sync
```

A status renamed in config and applied leaves items where they were — the
option keeps its id. A status added is empty until something is moved into it
with `board set`.

## What belongs here and what does not

Shape only: columns, fields, options, saved tabs. Which item sits in which
column is work, not shape — that is `board set`, in the work skill.

Creating the project itself is the same verb: with no board at all,
`board init` writes the config and applies it in one go.
